[Home](index.qmd)

The final set contains ten papers. Following group review, the revised selection includes Lazaridis et al. (2025) because it directly reconstructs Yamnaya formation, expansion and the proposed Indo-Anatolian connection. Citation counts were checked on 3–4 September 2026; the ordering below remains by Web of Science citation count within the revised set.

| Rank | Paper | Citations | Journal | Reported sample | Subtopics covered |
|---:|:---|---:|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | Haak et al. (2015). [Massive migration from the steppe was a source for Indo-European languages in Europe](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14317) | [1,352](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000356016700037&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 69 new individuals | Genetics,western migration,language inference |
| 2 | Allentoft et al. (2015). [Population genomics of Bronze Age Eurasia](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14507) | [1,141](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000356016700029&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 101 individuals | Genetics,western and eastern migration,language inference |
| 3 | Olalde et al. (2018). [The Beaker Phenomenon and the Genomic Transformation of Northwest Europe](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature25738) | [509](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000426763400040&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 400 individuals; 226 Beaker-associated | Culture,later western migration |
| 4 | Mathieson et al. (2018). [The genomic history of southeastern Europe](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature25778) | [505](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000426763400041&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 225 individuals; 216 new | Origins, genetics, southeastern migration |
| 5 | Wang et al. (2021). [Genomic insights into the formation of human populations in East Asia](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03336-2) | [330](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000627286100001&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 166 new individuals, 130 in main analysis | Genetics,eastern migration, language inference |
| 6 | Librado et al. (2021). [The origins and spread of domestic horses from the Western Eurasian steppes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-04018-9) | [268](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000709352200002&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 273 horses | Technology: horses and transport, mobility |
| 7 | Schroeder et al. (2019). [Unraveling ancestry, kinship, and violence in a Late Neolithic mass grave](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1820210116) | [139](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:000469280300023&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | PNAS | 15 individuals in the focal grave | Culture: kinship and burials in neighbouring communities |
| 8 | Saag et al. (2017). | 9 | Ringbauer et al. (2024). | 10 | Lazaridis et al. (2025). [The genetic origin of the Indo-Europeans](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08531-5) | [39](https://www.webofscience.com/api/gateway?GWVersion=2&SrcApp=paper-finder&SrcAuth=WosAPI&KeyUT=WOS:001415187000001&DestLinkType=FullRecord&DestApp=WOS_CPL) | Nature | 435 individuals; 367 newly reported and 68 with improved data | Origins, genetics, migration, language inference |


The set contains nine human ancient-DNA studies and one horse study. Language coverage is inferential. Independent linguistic analysis, metallurgy and wagons remain gaps.
